title: Zone Quality
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/0/body: A zone that price **hasn't come back to yet** is called a **fresh zone**. Many supply and demand traders see the **first return** to a zone as the best opportunity, because that's where the most unfilled orders are probably still waiting.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/1/body: Every time price returns to a zone, some of the orders get **used up**, like a wall that gets thinner with each hit. See how each bounce from this zone is **weaker** than the last, and the third test goes nearly to the distal line.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/2/prom: Since it formed, how many times has this chart's demand zone been tested?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/2/expl: After price left the base, two candles dipped into the zone with lower wicks and bounced. So the zone has been tested twice and isn't fresh anymore.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/3/prom: Tap the candle that returned to the supply zone for the first time (the first test).
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/3/expl: After the drop, this is the first candle whose wick entered the supply zone and closed below it. The last candle is the zone's second test.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/4/stat: In general, a zone that's been tested three times is stronger than a fresh zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/4/expl: In supply and demand, each test uses up some of the orders. That's why a fresh zone is usually higher quality, and lots of tests raise the odds of a break.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/5/prom: You have two demand zones: zone A hasn't been tested, and zone B has been tested twice. Everything else is equal. Which one comes first?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/5/opti: Zone A, because its orders haven't been used up
Zone B, because it's proven to work
No difference; only the zone's color matters
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/5/expl: With everything else equal, the fresh zone wins. Two earlier tests mean some of zone B's orders have probably been used up.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/6/titl: When is a zone no longer valid?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/6/body: If price pushes in close to the **distal line**, most of the orders are used up. **A candle close beyond the distal line** means the zone is **no longer valid**. Lower highs that keep pressing into a demand zone are also a sign it's weakening.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/6/tip: Let a worn-out zone go and look for the next fresh one.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/7/prom: This demand zone has been tested three times, the highs keep getting lower, and price is back inside the zone. Which move is more likely?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/7/expl: Each bounce from the zone got weaker, and the lower highs show sellers pressing. The zone's orders are probably used up, so a break down is more likely, though not certain.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/8/sent: A zone price hasn't returned to yet is a ___ zone, and its ___ test is usually the best opportunity.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l1/steps/8/expl: The first return to a fresh zone is where the most unfilled orders are probably waiting.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/0/titl: A strong leg-out: big orders' footprint
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/0/body: The **faster and bigger the candles** price leaves the base with, the bigger the imbalance was. **Long bodies with short wicks** and a big move away from the zone are signs of a **strong leg-out**.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/1/titl: Less time at the base is better
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/1/body: The number of base candles matters too. A **1 to 3 candle** base means orders got filled fast. Many traders see a long base (say **more than 6 candles**) as more of a range than a clean zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/1/exam: 1 base candle + exit with long candles
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/2/prom: There are two demand zones on this chart. Which one is stronger?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/2/expl: Zone "B" has just one base candle, and price shot away from it with two long candles. Zone "A" has six base candles and a slow, overlapping exit.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/3/prom: Which candle shows a powerful exit from the base? Tap it.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/3/expl: After two small base candles, this one pushed price up more than $1,000 with a very long body and a short wick. An explosive exit.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/4/prom: Based on time at the base and strength of the leg-out, which zone is better?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/4/opti: Two base candles, exit with long candles
Eight base candles, exit with long candles
Two base candles, exit with small, wicky candles
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/4/expl: A short base means orders filled fast, and an exit with long candles means a strong imbalance. This combo ticks both boxes.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/5/stat: Leg-out candles with small bodies and long wicks are a sign of a strong exit from the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/5/expl: Long wicks mean the other side was still active and price didn't get away easily. A strong leg-out has long bodies and short wicks.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/6/body: A simple way: check **how many times the base's height** price moved away after the base. If the leg-out **also breaks a previous high or key level**, many traders see the zone as more reliable, because buyers cleared resistance out of the way.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/7/prom: What's zone A's leg-out to base ratio, and which zone is stronger?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/7/expl: 48 ÷ 8 = 6x for A, but 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5x for B. Zone A made a much bigger move from a narrower base.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l2/steps/8/pair: The move before reaching the base
A short pause with small candles
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/0/titl: Why do higher timeframes matter more?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/0/body: A daily or weekly zone is built from **far more orders** than a 15-minute zone, and more traders can see it. That's why reactions to **higher timeframe zones** are usually bigger and more reliable.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/1/body: A daily zone can be wide and make your stop loss big. A common approach: when price reaches the **daily zone**, find a smaller zone **inside it** on a **lower timeframe** for a more precise entry and a smaller stop loss.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/1/tip: A smaller stop loss means a better reward-to-risk ratio for the same dollar risk.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/2/prom: Price has entered a daily demand zone. On the 15-minute chart, there's a small supply zone inside that area. What's the most sensible plan?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/2/opti: Look for a buy signal on the lower timeframe
Sell right away off the 15-minute supply zone
Ignore the daily zone because it's too wide
Buy with no stop loss, since the daily zone is strong
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/2/expl: The higher timeframe zone carries more weight. A small supply zone inside daily demand is probably weak, so we look for a buy setup in line with the daily zone, with a stop loss.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/3/prom: The wide "Daily" area is a higher timeframe demand zone. To buy with higher timeframe backing, which 1H zone is better?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/3/expl: Zone "A" formed inside the daily demand zone, so the two timeframes agree. Zone "B" is just a lone 1H zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/4/prom: Put the steps of top-down analysis for a zone trade in order.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/4/item: Wait for price to reach that zone
Find a smaller zone on a lower timeframe
Set entry and stop loss with the small zone
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/4/expl: The higher timeframe gives the big picture and direction; the lower timeframe gives a precise entry. Patience first, then the details.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/5/stat: A 5-minute supply zone can usually stop a move that started from a weekly demand zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/5/expl: A 5-minute zone has very few orders compared to a weekly zone. The higher timeframe zone usually wins that tug-of-war.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/6/body: Now put it all together: **freshness**, **leg-out strength**, **little time at the base** and **alignment with the higher timeframe**. A zone that ticks most of these boxes is worth waiting for.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/6/tip: You also need room between the zone and your target. If an opposing zone is too close, your reward shrinks.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/7/prom: By the checklist, which demand zone is higher quality?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/7/opti: Daily, fresh, one base candle, explosive exit
Daily, tested three times, slow exit
1H, against the daily trend, tested twice
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/7/expl: The first option ticks every box: higher timeframe, fresh, short base and a strong exit. Each of the others has at least one serious weakness.
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/8/prom: On the daily chart, gold has returned to its fresh demand zone and formed a bullish engulfing. Which move is more likely?
lessons/supply-demand-u2-l3/steps/8/expl: A fresh daily zone with a strong exit, an uptrend and a bullish engulfing inside the zone all favor buyers. A move up is more likely; a sensible stop loss goes below the zone's distal line.
